sn22.53:1.2: “Bhikkhus, one who is engaged is unliberated; one who is disengaged is liberated.
sn22.53:1.3: Consciousness, bhikkhus, while standing, might stand engaged with form; based upon form, established upon form, with a sprinkling of delight, it might come to growth, increase, and expansion.
sn22.53:1.4: Or consciousness, while standing, might stand engaged with feeling …
sn22.53:1.6: engaged with volitional formations; based upon volitional formations, established upon volitional formations, with a sprinkling of delight, it might come to growth, increase, and expansion.
sn22.53:2.2: ‘Apart from form, apart from feeling, apart from perception, apart from volitional formations, I will make known the coming and going of consciousness, its passing away and rebirth, its growth, increase, and expansion’—that is impossible.
sn22.53:3.1: “Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu has abandoned lust for the form element,
sn22.53:3.2: with the abandoning of lust the basis is cut off: there is no support for the establishing of consciousness.
sn22.53:3.3: If he has abandoned lust for the feeling element …
sn22.53:3.7: with the abandoning of lust the basis is cut off: there is no support for the establishing of consciousness.
sn22.53:3.8: “When that consciousness is unestablished, not coming to growth, nongenerative, it is liberated.
sn22.53:3.9: By being liberated, it is steady; by being steady, it is content; by being content, he is not agitated. Being unagitated, he personally attains Nibbāna.
sn22.53:3.10: He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’”
